subject: Dedicated capacity: traffic orchestration & token-sample request
message_1_body:
Hi Hiro,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — the latency numbers and cost controls looked compelling. We want to design the first reserved pool for our customer-facing assistant and need help sizing it before the contract. Can you confirm the best way to share a representative token/sample export?

High-level traffic notes from our side: 
- Peak window: 11:30–13:30 PT weekdays (user-facing chat).
- Avg session: 1.8 turns, median prompt 120 tokens, median response 220 tokens.
- Estimated 2,200 concurrent active sessions during peak (this is an early estimate).
- Some heavier API callers hit batch requests for report generation (~500 concurrent short jobs, avg prompt 40 tokens, response 1,200 tokens).

Questions:
1) Does Redwood prefer a CSV with one row per request (prompt_tokens, response_tokens, timestamp, route) or a sampling of HTTP logs?
2) How much historical telemetry do you need to produce a confident dedicated-sizing recommendation?
3) Any specific guidance on annotating variance (burst vs sustained) so sizing accounts for tail load?

Attaching a tiny sample (3 rows) for quick sanity check. Will follow up with a larger export if that format works.

— Chris
Chris Park
Head of Platform, QuantifyAI
[Attachment: quantify-token-sample.csv (csv)]
message_2_subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: initial traffic sketch
message_2_body:
Hi Chris — great to hear, glad the demo landed. Short answers first, then a suggested template.

1) CSV with one row per request is ideal. Required columns we use: timestamp (ISO8601), route/id, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, latency_ms (if available), caller_type (human/batch), and an optional request_id.
2) 7–14 days of representative telemetry usually gives a solid sizing baseline; include at least two peak days if you have them. For seasonal apps, call that out.
3) Annotate bursts with a boolean (is_burst) and include a running 1-minute concurrency metric if possible. We use that to model autoscaling and burst pools.

I'll attach a short template and a checklist. Karthik, can you take the lead on mapping their token mix to GPU SKU assumptions (we should run their 1,200-token responses through the p99 latency model)?

Next step: Chris, if you can share a 14-day sample (anonymized is fine) we will run a preliminary sizing and propose a two-tier reserved configuration (baseline + burst pool) and an expected cost delta. We can commit to a call next week to walk the results.

Thanks,
Hiro Tanaka
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-token-template.csv; Attachment: sizer-checklist.pdf]
message_3_subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: initial traffic sketch
message_3_body:
Chris — quick technical note from capacity planning:

Given the mix you described, two bucket approach looks right:
- Baseline pool sized for sustained sessions (~2,200 concurrent short-chat sessions at median lengths).
- Burst/Batch pool for heavy report jobs (the 500 concurrent long responses).

A few specifics I'll model once we have the token sample:
- Model variant: recommend testing both a quantized 8-bit variant and a mixed-precision 16-bit for the report path; throughput vs latency tradeoffs differ.
- KV-cache hit-rate: if you have a high proportion of short prompts with repetitive prefixes, effective token cost can drop significantly — include prefix_id if possible.
- Tail tolerance: we'll simulate a 5–10x call spike for a 5 minute window to size burst capacity and autoscale guardrails.

If you can anonymize and drop PII, send the CSV to my team and cc Hiro. We'll aim to return a draft capacity plan within 3 business days.

— Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer — Redwood Inference
message_4_subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: initial traffic sketch
message_4_body:
Thanks Hiro/Karthik — attaching the 14-day anonymized export and a short note on burst triggers. We've removed user_id and replaced with session_hash.

Attachments: quantify-token-sample.csv (full 14-day export), MAP-draft.pdf (mutual action plan we're hoping to align on).

Quick asks before you run the model:
- Please flag any columns you need changed/expanded.
- If we need to capture 1-minute concurrency and we don't have that, tell us an acceptable proxy (we can provide per-second request timestamps).
- Can you include a rough cost delta estimate for: (a) baseline-only reserved pool and (b) baseline + burst pool (with 10-minute autoscale window)?

Happy to sync on Monday morning PT for 30 minutes to walk the output.

— Chris
[Attachment: quantify-token-sample.csv; Attachment: MAP-draft.pdf]
